newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraq Kurd chief, U.S. official hold talks.
newsitem.headline: Iraq Kurd chief, U.S. official hold talks.

text.p: The Iraqi Kurdish leader who forged an alliance with Baghdad last month held talks in Turkey with a senior U.S. official on Wednesday on the altered power balance in northern Iraq, a source close to the talks said.

The source said Kurdish warlord Massoud Barzani, who seized control of northern Iraq with military help from Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, met U.S. State Department official Robert Pelletreau for several hours at a secret location in Ankara.

"The meeting is finished," the source said. He described the talks, billed in advance as a tough session, as "very successful" but gave few more details. He said a British diplomat and Turkish officials were present as observers.
Washington had been expected to try to dissuade Barzani from further cooperation with Saddam in a bid to pick up the pieces of its shattered policy on north Iraq.
"The Americans will want assurances that Saddam will not take over northern Iraq," a Western diplomatic source said ahead of the meeting.
Barzani's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) joined forces with Iraqi troops and tanks to take a key Kurdish city late last month, prompting U.S. missile strikes against southern Iraq.
Barzani has said he turned to Saddam for help against alleged Iranian-backed Kurdish rivals because the United States had failed to intervene to stop the Kurdish infighting.

A KDP spokesman said on Tuesday that Barzani planned to tell Pelletreau that his alliance with Baghdad was only temporary and that he wanted the Western allies to continue an air operation, based in Turkey, to protect the Kurds from Saddam.
Baghdad's involvement in the Kurdish feud has raised doubts on the effectiveness of the no-fly zone over northern Iraq.
"Mr Barzani's relationship with Saddam Hussein cannot be in the long-term interest of his people or himself," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Tuesday.

Barzani met Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller earlier on Wednesday but then gave reporters the slip in a car chase through Ankara on his way to the meeting with Pelletreau, the assistant secretary of state for near eastern affairs.
Washington has pulled back military, aid and intelligence operations from Iraq, fearing Barzani's new ties to the central government in Baghdad would put U.S. personnel and their local staff at risk.

European Union representatives are to meet Barzani in Ankara on Thursday to seek guarantees that he can protect aid organisations in northern Iraq affiliated to the EU from any attack by Baghdad, Turkey's Anatolian news agency said.
Diplomats say the number of Kurds and their relatives working for EU-subsidised aid agencies who have have asked to flee the region in recent weeks reaches into the thousands.
Barzani and Ciller discussed security on the Turkish-Iraq border earlier in the day.

Turkey says instability in northern Iraq plays into the hands of its own separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), which uses bases there, but Ankara has yet to unveil details of a proposed security zone in northern Iraq to halt rebel border violations.
